title: End-to-End Testing AI UX with Microsoft Playwright
description: Test React streaming chat interfaces, token rendering, cancellation controls, and tool approval modals with Playwright.

data.text: E2E Testing Challenges in AI User Experiences

Testing AI web interfaces end-to-end introduces unique challenges compared to standard CRUD apps. Streaming responses emit incremental chunks over Server-Sent Events, auto-scrolling dynamically adjusts the viewport, tool execution badges change state from 'pending' to 'approved' to 'completed', and the model's text can vary between runs. Microsoft Playwright provides the automation engine to test these dynamic asynchronous UI flows reliably.
Testing Streaming Chat & Abort Controls with Playwright

The Playwright test below navigates to the chat interface, enters a prompt, asserts that tokens stream into view, and verifies that clicking the 'Stop Generating' button aborts the stream and re-enables input.

data.text: Mocking Network SSE Streams in Playwright

To keep CI pipelines fast and prevent burning cloud tokens on every pull request, intercept the /api/chat endpoint using page.route() in Playwright to stream predetermined mock token chunks with precise timing delays.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Playwright automates end-to-end user journeys across modern React streaming AI interfaces
Test streaming edge cases: aborting mid-stream with Stop buttons, connection errors, and auto-scroll
Verify that Human-in-the-Loop tool approval modals correctly pause and resume workflows
Intercept and mock SSE /api/chat network routes for fast, deterministic, cost-free CI testing
Assert on semantic elements (e.g. data-testid or role attributes) rather than brittle CSS selectors
data.takeaway: E2E testing with Playwright verifies the complete human experience of your AI application, ensuring streaming controls, citations, and approval flows perform flawlessly in production.
